svg.text: -t
F09 · Threshold alarm
A sensor switches an output
BTEC First · ages 14–16
The thermistor and fixed resistor make a temperature-dependent voltage.
The comparator compares it with a reference; the transistor supplies the
LED current.
Your investigation
Predict which temperature direction turns the LED on. Change
Temperature, rerun, then change the reference. Explain why a real alarm
may need hysteresis.
This activity
Combine a sensor-equivalent input, comparator/transistor and LED load.
Set a target threshold and compare predicted switching with measured
sensor values. This is one possible implementation of the unit's design
work.
Getting started
Open the Simulation tab and press Run. Select a source or component to
see its values. Read the labelled signals, then change one quantity at a
time. Equal net labels identify connected points.
Raise the NTC Temperature above 25 °C and rerun. The falling sensor
voltage switches the comparator, then the transistor drives the LED.
Adjust THRESHOLD to choose the switching temperature.
Explain:
What changed, and why? Use your readings as evidence.
The model predicts electrical behaviour; it does not replace real practical
measurements.
